title: Persisted environment processes require config-specific ownership
summary: Status and cleanup share wide process inspection of the pinned wrangler launch and exact environment-derived config/state arguments. Logbooks additionally distinguish state directories despite their shared package config. Stale or foreign PID markers never authorize a termination signal.
proves: Real detached harmless sentinels survive stale-marker down and up; lookalike wrangler text and forged path hints never report an environment up. Actual ordinary wrangler and logbook lifecycles still report up and stop their own groups, while another environment using a different config or state remains alive. Existing environment lifecycle tests and static/generation checks pass. No process APIs or services are mocked.

captions.01-fails-first: Baseline kills an unrelated sentinel and misreports a wrangler-word lookalike as up.
captions.02-ownership-tests: Five real process/workerd ownership guards, including ordinary and logbook lifecycle.
captions.03-environment-regressions: Existing environment lifecycle and process ownership guards together.
captions.04-workspace-checks: Nx reset/sync, lint/typecheck and generated drift checks.
captions.05-final-ownership: All nine ownership/lifecycle guards, with direct OS confirmation that owned ordinary/logbook groups stopped.
captions.06-final-static: Final test-file lint/typecheck and generated drift check.
captions.04-integrated-ownership: Nine real process/environment lifecycle tests pass after integration; unrelated processes survive and genuine ordinary/logbook groups stop.
